title: The Bhagavad Gita: The Song of the Lord
subtitle: As Sanjaya told it to the blind king
hook_line: Before a single arrow flies, the finest archer of his age lets his bow fall; in a dark hall, a blind king asks what happened on that field.

description:
Kurukshetra, before sunrise. Two armies of one family, one chariot between them, and before a single arrow flies, the finest archer of his age lets his bow fall. What his charioteer, Krishna, tells him is the Bhagavad Gita, the Song of the Lord.

This film tells all eighteen chapters the way the Gita itself is framed: through Sanjaya, who by the sage Vyasa's grace can see the battlefield, describing it to the blind king Dhritarashtra. Every verse is on screen with its chapter and verse, in Devanagari, transliteration and English. The Sanskrit is shown, not recited. English verses are quoted from Shri Purohit Swami (1935, edited text); Gita 4.7 and 13.34 are quoted from Swami Sivananda (1949, edited text). Chapter 13 is numbered as in our source, which counts Arjuna's opening question as 13.1, so our 13.28 and 13.34 are 13.27 and 13.33 in 700-verse editions such as Gita Press.

A note on how we work. Every verse is shown with its chapter and verse, in a public-domain translation named on screen. Our own reading is marked OUR NOTE. The pictures are drawn in code, the voice is synthetic, and nothing here speaks for God.

beats.note: [≈1:08] 1.24 (Krishna 'drew up His bright chariot in the midst between the two armies') is shown, not narrated. FACT-CHECK FIX: Purohit's leading words 'Raising his bow, he spoke this to the Lord Shri Krishna: O Infallible Lord of the earth!' are dropped; the picture shows the raised bow instead. 'Lord of the earth' is not Arjuna's: in the Sanskrit, mahī-pate is Sanjaya's address to the blind king (corpus 1.21, Devanagari line 1: हृषीकेशं तदा वाक्यमिदमाह महीपते, 'then, O lord of the earth, he spoke these words to Hrishikesha'; Sivananda's 1.20 has it so, 'O Lord of the Earth', to the king). Arjuna's own words are only senayor ubhayor madhye rathaṁ sthāpaya me 'chyuta; Purohit's edited text fuses his achyuta ('O Infallible') with the king's title, so the one cannot be kept without the other. Do not put 'Infallible' back by hand: the line must stay a contiguous excerpt. Arjuna's voice: young, strong, a warrior's confidence that breaks within a minute.

beats.speaker: KRISHNA

scene.light: pre-dawn indigo; a thin saffron rim behind the chariot; sun below the horizon

beats.say: There, Arjuna noticed fathers, grandfathers, uncles, cousins, sons, grandsons, teachers, and friends.

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: He came to face an enemy. He finds a family.

scene.light: pre-dawn indigo; a thin saffron rim behind the chariot; sun below the horizon

beats.speaker: ARJUNA

scene.light: pre-dawn indigo; a thin saffron rim behind the chariot; sun below the horizon; cold

beats.note: [≈1:27] Pays off the cold open: the whole verse, in its place. The voice cracks; the drone thins to a single string.

beats.speaker: ARJUNA
beats.say: I do not crave victory, nor a kingdom, nor any pleasure. What would a kingdom, happiness, or life be to me?

scene.light: pre-dawn indigo; a thin saffron rim behind the chariot; sun below the horizon; cold

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Having spoken thus, Arjuna sank into the seat of his chariot, discarding his bow and arrow, overwhelmed with grief in the midst of the armies.

scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 1.47 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Two. The yoga of knowledge.
beats.note: [≈1:56] The card carries CHAPTER N and the Devanagari numeral; the voice says only the numeral and the name.

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Krishna's answer is stern at first. In effect: stand up; this weakness is unworthy of you.

scene.light: saffron rim a little wider; backlit glow; sun below the horizon; hard side light
scene.plate: SANJAYA'S PARAPHRASE · GITA 2.2-2.3

beats.note: [≈2:00] Paraphrase of 2.2-2.3, flagged on screen. Purohit's own wording there ('unmanliness', 'effeminacy') is deliberately not quoted.

beats.speaker: ARJUNA
beats.say: My heart is oppressed with pity, and my mind is confused as to what my duty is. Therefore, my Lord, tell me what is best for my spiritual welfare, for I am Your disciple. Please direct me, I pray.

scene.light: saffron rim a little wider; backlit glow; sun below the horizon; soft
scene.detail: Arjuna's silhouette looks up toward Krishna
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.7 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.note: [≈2:07] The hinge of the whole Gita: the friend asks to be taught. Let the last four words fall quietly.

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: A friend has become a teacher. Arjuna tells him he will not fight, and falls silent. And there, between the two armies, Krishna smiles.

scene.light: saffron rim a little wider; backlit glow; sun below the horizon; warm gold rises behind Krishna

beats.note: [≈2:22] Narration of 2.9-2.10 (Purohit 2.10: 'with a gracious smile'). The smile is never drawn: the light warms instead. Flute motif returns.

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: There was never a time when I was not, nor you, nor these princes were not; there will never be a time when we shall cease to exist.

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: As a man discards his threadbare robes and puts on new ones, so the Spirit throws off its worn-out bodies and takes on fresh ones.

beats.say: You have only the right to work, but none to the fruit of it. Let not the fruit of your action be your motive; nor be you enamored of inaction.

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Then he describes a mind that stands still: one that draws in its senses as a tortoise draws in its limbs.

scene.kind: a tortoise drawing in its limbs

scene.kind: rivers entering the ocean

scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.70 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: A sea that never rises. I wish you could see it, my king. Krishna has said that action is far below a mind fixed on the Divine; and still he tells Arjuna to fight.

scene.detail: the king's face stays in shadow; only the lamp moves
scene.plate: SANJAYA'S PARAPHRASE · GITA 2.49

beats.note: [≈3:31] The king's blindness, gently; then the doubt that opens chapter 3. Reports 2.49 (Purohit: 'Physical action is far inferior to an intellect concentrated on the Divine') and the 'fight' of 2.18 and 2.37. Grafted from the 'arjuna' draft (c02b13).

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Three. The yoga of action.
beats.note: [≈3:45] The card carries CHAPTER N and the Devanagari numeral; the voice says only the numeral and the name.

beats.speaker: ARJUNA
beats.say: My Lord! If wisdom is superior to action, why do you advise me to engage in this terrible fight?

scene.light: saffron rim a little wider; backlit glow; sun below the horizon

beats.say: No one, Krishna answers, can stop acting:

scene.light: saffron rim a little wider; backlit glow; sun below the horizon

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: He cannot remain inactive even for a moment, for the qualities of Nature will compel him to act, whether he wills it or not.

scene.light: saffron rim a little wider; backlit glow; sun below the horizon
scene.detail: nothing on the field is still: wind in a thousand banners, the horses' flanks rising and falling, dust turning in the light

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: In this world, people are fettered by their actions, unless they are performed as a sacrifice. Therefore, O Arjuna, let your actions be done without attachment, as a sacrifice only.

scene.english: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action

beats.say: Then Krishna says something no charioteer could say: long ago, he taught this to Vivasvan, the Sun. Arjuna objects that Krishna was born in their own time.

beats.say: I have been born again and again, from time to time; thou too, O Arjuna! My births are known to me, but yours are unknown to you.

scene.detail: behind the chariot, faint concentric rings of light, like ripples, each one an age; never a figure
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 4.5 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.say: Five. Renunciation.
beats.note: [≈5:06] The card carries CHAPTER N and the Devanagari numeral; the voice says only the numeral and the name.

beats.speaker: ARJUNA
beats.say: At one moment, You praise renunciation of action; at another, You praise right action. Tell me truly, I pray, which of these is more conducive to my highest welfare?

scene.light: saffron rim a little wider; backlit glow; sun below the horizon
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 5.1 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.note: [≈5:09] Leading 'Arjuna said: My Lord!' dropped.

beats.say: Six. Meditation.
beats.note: [≈5:43] The card carries CHAPTER N and the Devanagari numeral; the voice says only the numeral and the name.

beats.say: The wise man who has conquered his mind and is absorbed in the Self is like a lamp that does not flicker, as it stands sheltered from every wind.

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: My beloved child! There is no destruction for him, either in this world or the next. No evil fate awaits him who treads the path of righteousness.

scene.kind: a lamp in a windless place (relit)

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Seven. Knowledge and realisation.
beats.note: [≈6:28] The card carries CHAPTER N and the Devanagari numeral; the voice says only the numeral and the name.

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Now Krishna turns from the seeker to himself: to what holds the whole world together.

scene.light: rose and saffron rim, brighter; sun still hidden; the light around Krishna slightly brighter than the sky

beats.say: O Arjuna! There is nothing higher than Me; all is strung on Me like rows of pearls on a thread.

beats.say: I am the fragrance of the earth, the brilliance of fire, the life force in all beings, and the austerity of ascetics.

scene.kind: pearls on a thread (the thread revealed)
scene.detail: first rain on dry earth; a fire's glow; breath in cold air; a seated ascetic as a far silhouette; the gold thread runs through each image
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 7.9 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.say: Eight. The imperishable.
beats.note: [≈6:57] The card carries CHAPTER N and the Devanagari numeral; the voice says only the numeral and the name.

beats.speaker: ARJUNA
beats.say: how may those who have learned self-control come to the knowledge of Thee at the time of death?

scene.view: the battlefield seen from the chariot
scene.light: rose and saffron rim, brighter; sun still hidden
scene.detail: ten thousand spears at rest; a crow crossing the glow
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 8.2 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: Whosoever, at the time of death, thinks only of Me and, thinking thus, leaves the body and goes forth, will assuredly know Me.

scene.kind: a flame returning to the sun

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: Therefore, always meditate on Me and fight; if your mind and reason are fixed on Me, you will surely come to Me.

scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 8.7 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

scene.detail: the king's head lifts a little

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Nine. The royal secret.
beats.note: [≈7:34] The card carries CHAPTER N and the Devanagari numeral; the voice says only the numeral and the name.

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: Whatever a person offers to Me, be it a leaf, flower, fruit, or water, I accept it, for it is offered with devotion and a pure mind.

scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 9.26 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: A leaf. A flower. A little water. Anyone on earth could bring him that.

scene.detail: a single marigold petal on the floor of the hall, in the lamplight

beats.note: [≈7:50] Sanjaya's reflection on 9.26, not a quotation.

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you sacrifice and give, whatever austerities you practice, do all as an offering to Me.

scene.detail: the fallen Gandiva on the chariot floor, lit for a moment as if it were an offering; no added words
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 9.27 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.note: [≈7:56] Answers c08b05. Image grafted from the 'arjuna' draft (c09b03).

beats.say: Ten. The divine glories.

beats.say: Then, in effect, he names himself in the best of everything: among things that never move, the Himalaya; among rivers, the Ganges; among letters, A; and among secrets, silence.

scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 11.8 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Could a thousand suns blaze forth together, it would be but a faint reflection of the radiance of the Lord God.

beats.speaker: ARJUNA
beats.say: I see You, infinite in form, with faces, eyes, and limbs everywhere; with no beginning, middle, or end.

scene.detail: galaxies, rivers, mountains, cities, flocks, all turning inside the light, folding into each other; 'faces, eyes and limbs' are never drawn: only multitudes of points of light
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 11.16 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Then the vision turns, my king. In that fire Arjuna sees your sons, and Bhishma, and Drona, rushing in.

scene.detail: the gold deepens to red; far below, the two armies on the field, tiny, streaming toward the light like sparks

beats.note: [≈9:20] Narration of 11.26-11.27 (true to the text: 'All these sons of Dhritarashtra ... Bheeshma, Drona'). 'Your sons': the sentence the blind king hears about his own children. 11.26 also names 'the other warrior chiefs on our side' (sahāsmadīyair api yodha-mukhyaiḥ): Sanjaya names only the king's own, which is selective, not false, so the picture keeps BOTH armies streaming in. Drone drops a fifth, darker.

beats.speaker: ARJUNA
beats.say: As rivers in flood surge furiously towards the ocean, so these heroes, the greatest among men, fling themselves into Thy flaming mouths.

scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 11.28 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.note: [≈9:28] Pays off c02b09: the same image, now terrible. 'Mouths' are rendered only as fire.

beats.speaker: ARJUNA
beats.say: Tell me then, who are You, who wears this dreadful form?

scene.detail: the light at its most overwhelming; a small dark silhouette of Arjuna, kneeling, at the bottom of the frame

beats.speaker: KRISHNA

beats.say: Whatever I have said to you in rashness, taking you only as a friend and addressing you as “O Krishna! O Yadava! O Friend!” in thoughtless familiarity, without understanding your greatness;

scene.kind: the friend remembered

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Arjuna asks which seeker is best. In effect, Krishna answers: fix your mind on me. If you cannot, practise. If you cannot practise, work for my sake. And if even that is too much, let go of the fruit of what you do.

scene.kind: a stair of lamps

scene.detail: ghat steps descending to a river before sunrise; a lamp on every step; each 'if you cannot' moves the camera one step lower, and every step is still lit

beats.speaker: KRISHNA

beats.say: Thirteen. The field and its knower.
beats.note: [≈11:37] The card carries CHAPTER N and the Devanagari numeral; the voice says only the numeral and the name.

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Krishna calls the body kshetra, a field, and the one who knows it kshetrajna, the knower of the field. Kshetra, my king: the word that opened your question.

scene.kind: the field and its knower

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: He who can see the Supreme Lord in all beings, the Imperishable amidst the perishable, he is the one who truly sees.

scene.en_text: He who can see the Supreme Lord in all beings, the Imperishable amidst the perishable, he is the one who truly sees.
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 13.28 (13.27 IN 700-VERSE EDITIONS) · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: Just as the one sun illuminates the entire world, so too does the Lord of the field (Supreme Self) illuminate the entire field, O Arjuna.

scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 13.34 (13.33 IN 700-VERSE EDITIONS) · AFTER SWAMI SIVANANDA, 1949 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.note: [≈12:02] NUMBERING: 13.33 in 700-verse editions; the plate says so. TRANSLATION NOTE: Purohit widens the Sanskrit here. kṣhetraṁ kṣhetrī tathā kṛitsnaṁ prakāśhayati is 'so the knower of the field lights the whole field' (Sivananda: 'the Lord of the field (Supreme Self) illuminate the entire field'); Purohit has 'the Lord illuminates the entire universe'. Kept, as Purohit's exact and usable words; a Sivananda swap would tie the verse to the chapter's title, and is AK's call (it would add a second Sivananda credit).

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: But what ties the knower to the field? Krishna names three cords.

scene.light: gold just under the horizon; sky almost day; sun still hidden

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Fourteen. The three qualities.
beats.note: [≈12:14] The card carries CHAPTER N and the Devanagari numeral; the voice says only the numeral and the name.

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: Purity, passion, and ignorance are the qualities that the law of nature brings forth. They fetter the free spirit in all beings.

scene.kind: three lights for the three gunas

scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 14.5 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Sattva, rajas, tamas: a clear light, a restless flame, a heavy dark. All three can bind, he says, even the bright one. How, then, does anyone go free?

scene.kind: three lights for the three gunas
scene.detail: on 'even the bright one' the camera finds the thread tied to the white flame too

beats.note: [≈12:29] 'Even the bright one' is from 14.6 (purity 'binds one with its yearning for happiness and illumination'). The light, flame and dark images are our picture, drawn from 14.6-14.8 and 14.11-14.13 (Purohit 14.11 'the light of knowledge', 14.12 'the impulse to act', 14.13 'Darkness'). The closing question is grafted from the 'arjuna' draft (c14b03). TTS: SUT-va, RA-jas, TA-mas.

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: And he who serves Me alone, with unwavering devotion, shall overcome the Qualities and become one with the Eternal.

scene.kind: three lights for the three gunas (released)

scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 14.26 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Fifteen. The supreme person.
beats.note: [≈12:48] The card carries CHAPTER N and the Devanagari numeral; the voice says only the numeral and the name.

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Now he speaks of a tree that grows upside down: the sacred ashvattha, roots above, in the Highest, branches hanging into our world. It must be hewn down, he says, with the sharp axe of non-attachment.

scene.kind: the upside-down ashvattha tree
scene.detail: a vast fig tree hangs from a sky of light, roots above, branches and leaves trailing down into a world of rivers and cities; on 'axe' a single clean stroke of light cuts through the trunk
scene.plate: SANJAYA'S PARAPHRASE · GITA 15.1-15.3

beats.note: [≈12:52] Reported speech of 15.1-15.3, not a quotation. The image follows the Sanskrit urdhva-mulam adhah-shakham ashvattham (roots above, branches below), not Purohit's 'seed above'. 'Hewn down by the sharp axe of non-attachment' is Purohit's 15.3 phrase, reported with 'he says'; 15.3 states no exclusivity, so the draft's 'Only one blade can cut it' is gone. FACT-CHECK FIX: 'he shows Arjuna a tree' became 'he speaks of a tree' (15.1 prāhuḥ, 'they speak of'; this is a teaching, not a vision like chapter 11), and 'roots in heaven' became 'roots above, in the Highest' (ūrdhva-mūlam, 'roots above'; Purohit 15.1 'in the Highest'): 'heaven' would suggest svarga, which the verse does not say. beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: Neither the sun, nor the moon, nor fire shines there. Those who go there never come back. For, O Arjuna, that is my celestial home!

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Sixteen. The divine and the demonic.
beats.note: [≈13:19] The card carries CHAPTER N and the Devanagari numeral; the voice says only the numeral and the name.

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Two roads. Along one, he names the divine qualities: fearlessness first, then truth, compassion, forgiveness, freedom from hate. Along the other: hypocrisy, pride, cruelty.

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: Godly qualities lead to liberation; godless ones lead to bondage. Do not be anxious, Prince! You have the Godly qualities.

scene.light: gold just under the horizon; sky almost day; sun still hidden; warm
scene.detail: Krishna's hand rests on Arjuna's shoulder in silhouette
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 16.5 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: The gates of hell are three: lust, wrath, and avarice; they destroy the Self, so avoid them.

scene.kind: two roads (the three gates)
scene.detail: on the shadow road, three dark gateways one behind another; the chariot's road turns away from them toward the light
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 16.21 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Do not be anxious, he tells Arjuna. He will say it again, at the very end.

scene.light: gold just under the horizon; sky almost day; sun still hidden

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Seventeen. Three kinds of faith.
beats.note: [≈13:56] The card carries CHAPTER N and the Devanagari numeral; the voice says only the numeral and the name.

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: Every person's faith conforms to their nature. By nature, they are full of faith. They are, in fact, what their faith makes them.

scene.kind: three lights for the three gunas (as faith)
scene.detail: the three lamps of chapter 14 return, now each held in a different pair of hands
scene.overlay: यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः · yo yach-chhraddhaḥ sa eva saḥ (from the corpus, 17.3 line 2) in a card corner
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 17.3 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: Speech that hurts no one, that is true, pleasant to listen to, and beneficial, and the constant study of the scriptures—this is austerity of speech.

scene.en_text: Speech that hurts no one, that is true, pleasant to listen to, and beneficial, and the constant study of the scriptures—this is austerity of speech.

beats.say: The last chapter, my king. Arjuna asks what it truly means to renounce.

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: The duty that falls to one's lot of its own accord should not be abandoned, though it may have its defects. All acts are marred by defects, just as fire is obscured by smoke.

scene.en_text: Thus, I have revealed to you the truth, the mystery of mysteries. Having thought it over, you are free to act as you wish.

scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 18.63 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.note: [≈14:59] The film's quiet revelation: after everything, a choice. Full card.

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Free, my king. After everything, he leaves the choice to Arjuna. And then he speaks once more, as a friend.

scene.detail: the king lifts his face toward the voice

beats.note: [≈15:11] OUR NOTE: our reading of 18.63 as a handing-back of the choice. The draft's 'He does not command' is gone: 18.65-18.66, which follow, are commands. Wording after the 'lamps' draft (c18b04).

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: Listen to My last word once more, the deepest secret of all; you are My beloved, you are My friend, and I speak for your welfare.

scene.light: rim burning white-gold; sun about to break; the warmest light of the film
scene.detail: Krishna turned fully to Arjuna; the reins slack in one hand
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 18.64 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.note: [≈15:19] Quoted, not reported (grafted from the 'lamps' draft, c18b05): the payoff of the friend at the reins. 18.65 is cut for length; its 'you are My beloved' is already here.

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: Give up your earthly duties, surrender yourself to Me alone. Do not be anxious; I will absolve you from all your sins.

scene.en_text: Give up your earthly duties, surrender yourself to Me alone. Do not be anxious; I will absolve you from all your sins.

beats.note: [≈15:30] Sarva-dharman parityajya. One second of total silence before the line, a single bell after it, then hold the full card. Pays off c16b05: light मा शुचः (ma shucah), the same two words as 16.5; no line is added. Purohit's 'earthly duties' renders sarva-dharman; the transliteration shows the Sanskrit.

beats.speaker: KRISHNA
beats.say: O Arjuna, have you listened attentively to My words? Has your ignorance and delusion gone?

scene.light: rim burning white-gold; sun about to break
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 18.72 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.note: [≈15:41] Asked gently, almost smiling. Then one held breath of silence.

beats.speaker: ARJUNA
beats.say: My Lord! O Immutable One! My delusion has fled. By Your Grace, O Changeless One, the light has dawned. My doubts have been dispelled, and I stand before You ready to do Your will.

scene.light: the disc of the sun clears the horizon for the first time in the film, exactly on 'the light has dawned'; gold floods the field
scene.detail: Arjuna rises and lifts the Gandiva from the chariot floor; on 'ready to do Your will' it is raised into the sun
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 18.73 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.note: [≈15:48] 'Arjuna replied:' and the quotation marks dropped. Arjuna's strongest voice in the film. Pays off the cold open (p00b01), Krishna's 'stand up' (c02b02) and 'Be thou my instrument' (c11b11). The bow rising is staging: the verse says he stands ready; it does not describe the bow. Panchajanya's conch on the last word (staging too: the text sounds no conch here; Arjuna's own conch is Devadatta, 1.15).

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: As I recall again and again the exceeding beauty of the Lord, I am filled with amazement and joy.

scene.detail: first grey of morning at the high windows; a faint gold afterglow of the thousand suns on Sanjaya's silhouette
scene.plate: BHAGAVAD GITA 18.77 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.note: [≈16:03] Back in the hall: the frame closes. Pays off c11b03 ('So I saw it too').

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: You asked me what happened on that field, my king. You have not said a word since.

scene.detail: the king's silhouette, very still

beats.note: [≈16:11] True to the text: Dhritarashtra speaks only 1.1. Silence under the line.

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Wherever Lord Shri Krishna, the Prince of Wisdom, and Arjuna, the Great Archer, are, I am certain that good fortune, victory, happiness, and righteousness will follow.

beats.note: [≈16:19] The last verse of the Gita, Sanjaya's. Conch at the end of the line, then the drone alone; hold the card 4 s and let the conch ring out fully. For this king the verse is also the verdict on his sons: let the silence say it. The corpus's trailing '।।18.78।' marker is stripped from the card.

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: Eighteen chapters. Seven hundred verses. One conversation between two friends; and one of them held the reins.

scene.light: full morning sun over Kurukshetra
scene.detail: the chariot between the armies in full sunlight: four white horses, the pennant streaming, Arjuna standing with the bow raised, Krishna at the reins

beats.note: [≈16:33] Sanjaya's closing line (after the 'arjuna' draft's c19b04); 'one of them held the reins' answers c11b18, so the friend is not undersold. Seven hundred is the traditional count (the corpus has 701 because it counts 13.1). Then a single bell, then the disclosure.

beats.speaker: SANJAYA
beats.say: This was the Bhagavad Gita, as Sanjaya told it to the blind king.
